## What is `frontend/node_modules`?
`node_modules` is the folder where **all the libraries your project depends on** are installed.
---
### Simple analogy:
``` package.json = Shopping list npm install = Going to the store node_modules/ = Your kitchen pantry (all the ingredients) ```
---
### How it works:
**1. You define what you need in `package.json`:** ```json { "dependencies": { "next": "16.2.3", "react": "19.2.4", "react-dom": "19.2.4" } } ```
**2. You run `npm install` — it downloads everything into `node_modules/`:** ``` frontend/node_modules/ ├── next/ ← Next.js framework ├── react/ ← React library ├── react-dom/ ← React DOM rendering ├── typescript/ ← TypeScript compiler ├── tailwindcss/ ← CSS framework └── ... (hundreds more sub-dependencies) ```
---
### Key facts:
| Fact | Detail | |---|---| | **Size** | Usually 200MB–1GB+ | | **Edit it?** | Never — always auto-generated | | **In `.gitignore`?** | Yes — never pushed to GitHub | | **How to recreate** | Just run `npm install` | | **Safe to delete?** | Yes — `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` rebuilds it |
---
### Why it's never pushed to GitHub:
It can contain **hundreds of thousands of files** and is **huge in size**. Instead, only `package.json` is committed — anyone who clones the repo just runs `npm install` and gets the same packages.
``` # Your .gitignore already has: frontend/node_modules/ ← correctly ignored ```
---
### Summary:
``` node_modules/ = all the tools/libraries your code borrows from auto-downloaded, never edited, never committed ```
